text:
maria: quick heads-up — I opened a docs PR that combines the Dedicated provisioning quickstart with the autoscale policy examples. trying to get this into the config-ref before the community sync tomorrow. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482

kevin: thanks — skimmed. main question: did you keep the minimum-viable reserved pool example? we should avoid implying that reserved pools are required for all tenants. :thinking_face:

maria: yes — top of the file has a clear 'when to use dedicated vs hosted' callout. the reserved pool example is under "optional reserved pool". i also added a short migration checklist for teams moving from hosted to dedicated.

sam: can you paste the terraform snippet you added? i ran into subtle var name mismatches last time.

maria: pasted below — it's the minimal example i validated against the terraform provider v0.5.2. mind checking formatting for the handbook?

```
resource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "small" {
  name         = "team-small"
  gpu_type     = "A10G"
  reserved_gpu = 2
  isolation    = "tenant"
  labels = {
    cost_center = "ml-research"
  }
}

resource "redwood_autoscale_policy" "burst" {
  pool_id           = redwood_dedicated_pool.small.id
  target_utilization = 0.65
  min_replicas       = 1
  max_replicas       = 4
  cooldown_seconds   = 180
}
```

jordan: looks good. minor nit: in the runtime we call the isolation mode "tenant_isolated" not "tenant" — that mismatch will confuse teams copying the snippet.

maria: ugh, good catch. i'll update the snippet to use the runtime value and add a short note about what each isolation mode means.

kevin: also, SLA wording — the PR currently says "<99.9% uptime for preemptible tiers>" which read weird. maybe phrase as "preemptible tiers do not currently have an uptime SLA; applications should configure fallback routing to hosted or a lower-latency dedicated pool."

maria: agreed. i'll reword to the clearer wording and add an example policy block for fallback routing that references the routing config in the runbook.

sam: small doc QA — the autoscale examples mention "target_utilization" as 0.65 but our telemetry team suggests 0.7 for models with KV cache enabled. maybe add a note about tuning by model shape.

maria: adding a short table: default guidance for seq length <512 -> 0.7, long sequences -> 0.55, kv-cache heavy -> 0.75. i'll cite the perf playbook.

docs-bot: Added labels: docs, dedicated, autoscale. Requested reviewers: @kevin @sam @jordan.

jordan: I'll review after lunch. If no blockers, can we merge and do a quick 'docs release' sync to update the console links?

maria: yes — goal is to merge today. I'll also open a follow-up PR to extract the SDK snippet (python + TS) into the examples directory so we don't duplicate.

kevin: thumbs up from me for content once the isolation key and SLA wording are fixed. :thumbsup:

sam: quick nit for the handbook link — you reference /handbook/onboarding/dedicated but the actual path is /handbook/onboarding/dedicated-capacity. small link fix needed.

maria: thanks, fixing that too. i'll push an update in ~30m and ping the thread when the fixes are up. :rocket:
